newsitem.title: UK: Brown forecasts 3.25 percent GDP growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Brown forecasts 3.25 percent GDP growth in 1997.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown on Wednesday forecast the British economy will grow by 3.25 percent this year and 2.5 percent in 1998.
"The forecast is that GDP will grow by 3.25 percent this year and 2.5 percent next year before returning to its trend rate," Brown said in his budget speech to parliament.
In his last budget, Brown's predecessor Kenneth Clarke forecast GDP growth of 3.5 percent this year, falling to 3.0 percent in the first half of 1988.

Revised first quarter data for UK gross domestic product (GDP) showed the economy grew 0.9 percent compared with the fourth quarter of 1996 and at an annual rate of 3.1 percent, well above the trend rate of 2.25 to 2.5 percent. The economy is now in its sixth straight year of economic growth.
(A separate summary of key economic forecasts will run after Brown finishes his budget speech.)
